references.text: Reuse of the same logical structure and wording where Jesus states that the people have seen his signs, yet still do not believe.
Jesus points out that the people have seen his works, yet still hated him and did not believe, reflecting the contrast between sight and faith in John 6:36.
Jesus accuses his listeners of not having God's word in them because they do not believe in the one he sent, even though they have seen him.
Jesus asks why they do not believe in him, even though he speaks the truth they have seen and heard.
Jesus explains that they do not believe because they are not of his flock, even though they have seen his works.
The prophecy that the message about the Lord is not believed, even though the arm (God's revelation) has been revealed, as a direct parallel to the situation in John 6.
